BLOCKER: Put's `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE memory.owner = EXCLUDED.owner` plus `n == 0 → error` freezes every pre-0015 row (migration backfills `owner=''`), while the API always sends `Owner=principal`: legacy entries can never be upserted and now 500 with a misleading "belongs to another tenant/owner" message.

AC claims hybrid/vector-degradation tests, but `memory_test.go` only asserts the wrong-dimension error; no test covers FTS-only degradation, hybrid score merging, or migration 0015's optional-column behaviour — a core acceptance criterion is unverified.
MAJOR: Static `PF_MEMORY_PRINCIPAL` (default "admin") is the only principal: all requests share one owner, so private-ACL ownership and the "cross-user leakage" guarantee hold only in the store unit, not in the running API.
AC-required `user` and GET-level `embedding`/`acl_scope` params are never read by the handler, so hybrid search and per-user scoping are unreachable through `/memory`.
HNSW index is dead: ranking via `CASE WHEN ... 1 - (embedding <=> ...) END` in SELECT/ORDER BY prevents ANN plan selection, giving O(table) distance computation per query.
`Search` with empty `scope.TenantID` emits no tenant predicate, failing open unless RLS happens to be bound — the AC's "RLS plus explicit guard" pairing is conditional.
Non-ACL legacy `?source=` values now filter the new `source` column (always `''`) instead of `acl_scope`, silently returning nothing for previously valid callers.
MINOR: Down migration removes indexes/tsv but leaves `memory_kind_valid`/`memory_acl_valid` CHECK constraints, contradicting its own "only derived/index objects are removed" contract.
Validation paths (kind/acl/dimension) have no DB-free unit tests; everything skips when `PF_DB_DSN` is unset.
`log.Printf` for pgvector degradation bypasses structured logging/metrics — no counter for FTS-only fallback.
`formatVector`/`tsq` adds the query parameter twice in hybrid mode; harmless but signals unreviewed SQL assembly.
API returns raw `err.Error()` on Put/Search failures, leaking SQL/driver detail to clients.
`SET LOCAL lock_timeout` is a no-op if the migrator runs non-transactionally; non-concurrent `CREATE INDEX` takes a table lock.
NIT: `%g` can render `NaN`/`+Inf`, producing an invalid pgvector literal and an opaque SQL error.
`EmbeddingDim = 1536` is duplicated as a literal `vector(1536)` in the migration; drift would only surface at runtime.
Positive `hasVec` cache is never invalidated if the column/extension is later dropped.
SUMMARY: Solid substrate direction: parameterised SQL, server-side ACL predicates, fail-closed kinds, and a genuinely stock-Postgres-safe migration.
Top risks: legacy rows become un-upsertable (blocker), unverified hybrid/degradation AC, unreachable API vector/user params, and a static principal making owner-ACL largely symbolic.
Re-run precheck with the legacy-row upsert case and hybrid tests added before merge.
